To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the interresponse times that are reinforced by different terminal-link schedules can serve to distinguish between those schedules, and (b) the accuracy with which rats can distinguish between different schedules' reinforced response times is a positive function of the difference between the schedules' reinforced inter-response times.

the size of the difference between the terminal-link reinforced inter-response times of a tandem schedule and a comparison schedule is the best predictor of accuracy in the conditional-discrimination task.
the interresponse-times reinforced by tandem schedules and the interresponse times that are reinforced by random-interval schedules can serve as a cue for discriminating between these schedules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the interresponse time in discriminating between different schedules.
the ability of a single sample to discriminate between different schedules' reinforced response rates and interresponse times.
the ability of animals to use the interresponse times that are reinforced by different schedules to discriminate between the schedules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interresponse time reinforced by the terminal link in a tandem schedule is a cue that can be used to discriminate between tandem schedules.
the interresponse-time distributions produced by tandem and random-interval schedules are different, and that these differences are sufficient to support the discrimination of different schedules.
interresponse time is a discriminative stimulus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rats can discriminate between schedules on the basis of their terminal links' reinforcement functions.
rats' conditional discrimination between two different schedules is based on the temporal difference between schedules' reinforced inter-response times.
interresponse-time schedules can be discriminated by their interresponse-time values.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rats can learn to discriminate between schedules that differ in the interresponse times that they reinforce.
the interresponse time is an effective discriminative stimulus in the tandem schedule.
the temporal properties of schedules can serve as discriminative stimuli.
